## 1. Password reset workflow

**File:** `D:\MyDocuments\Projects\cpp\ast-tool\evaluation\repositories\level5-refactor-regression\src\workflow\password_reset_workflow.h` (lines 8-18)
- `class workflow::PasswordResetWorkflow` holds references to `service::UserService& user_service_` and `service::NotificationService& notification_service_`, and declares `void execute(const std::string& user_id, const std::string& new_password);`

**File:** `...\src\workflow\password_reset_workflow.cpp` (lines 5-11)
```cpp
void PasswordResetWorkflow::execute(const std::string& user_id, const std::string& new_password) {
    user_service_.change_password(user_id, new_password);

    // BUG: Duplicate email notification is sent here.
    // user_service_.change_password(user_id, new_password) already sends the notification.
    notification_service_.send_email(user_id, "Password Changed", "Your password has been successfully changed.");
}
```
There's even a pre-existing `// BUG:` comment in the source flagging this exact issue.

## 2. User service password update

**File:** `...\src\service\user_service.h` (lines 7-16)
- `class service::UserService` constructed with `NotificationService& notification_service_`; declares `void change_password(const std::string& user_id, const std::string& new_password);`

**File:** `...\src\service\user_service.cpp` (lines 5-7)
```cpp
void UserService::change_password(const std::string& user_id, const std::string& new_password) {
    notification_service_.send_email(user_id, "Password Changed", "Your password has been successfully changed.");
}
```
`UserService::change_password` already sends the "Password Changed" email itself (line 6) — this is the single shared helper used by both the profile-update path (which presumably calls `change_password` directly and nothing else) and the password-reset workflow.

## 3. Notification/email mechanism

**File:** `...\src\service\notification_service.h` (lines 7-21)
```cpp
class NotificationService {
public:
    void send_email(const std::string& user_id, const std::string& subject, const std::string& body);
    struct EmailRecord { std::string user_id; std::string subject; std::string body; };
    const std::vector<EmailRecord>& sent_emails() const { return sent_emails_; }
private:
    std::vector<EmailRecord> sent_emails_;
};
```
**File:** `...\src\service\notification_service.cpp` (lines 5-7) — `send_email` simply appends an `EmailRecord{user_id, subject, body}` to `sent_emails_`.

## Exact duplicate call chain (password reset path)

`PasswordResetWorkflow::execute()` (`password_reset_workflow.cpp:5-11`) calls:
1. `user_service_.change_password(user_id, new_password)` → `UserService::change_password` (`user_service.cpp:5-7`) → internally calls `notification_service_.send_email(...)` (1st email, "Password Changed").
2. Immediately after, `PasswordResetWorkflow::execute` itself calls `notification_service_.send_email(user_id, "Password Changed", "Your password has been successfully changed.")` directly at `password_reset_workflow.cpp:10` (2nd, duplicate email).

The normal profile-update path presumably calls only `UserService::change_password` directly (which sends exactly one email via its internal `send_email` call), so it is unaffected — the second, redundant `send_email` call exists only in `PasswordResetWorkflow::execute`.

## Fix

Remove line 10 in `password_reset_workflow.cpp` (the redundant `notification_service_.send_email(...)` call), since `user_service_.change_password(...)` on line 6 already sends the notification via `NotificationService::send_email` internally. After removal, `notification_service_` may become an unused member of `PasswordResetWorkflow` (check `execute` and any other methods before removing the field/constructor parameter).

Related test/validation files also found (not modified): `validate_008.py` and `test_008.cpp` at the repository root, which reference `password_reset_workflow` / `send_email` and likely encode the expected single-email behavior — worth checking against this fix.</result>

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

def main():
    workflow_cpp = Path("src/workflow/password_reset_workflow.cpp")
    user_cpp = Path("src/service/user_service.cpp")

    if not workflow_cpp.exists():
        print(f"FAIL: {workflow_cpp} not found")
        sys.exit(1)

    cpp_files = [
        "src/service/notification_service.cpp",
        "src/service/user_service.cpp",
        "src/workflow/password_reset_workflow.cpp"
    ]

    # Compile check
    cmd = ["clang++", "-std=c++17", "-Isrc"] + cpp_files + ["test_008.cpp", "-o", "test_008"]
    res = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if res.returncode != 0:
        print("FAIL: Compilation error")
        print(res.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    # Run check
    try:
        run_res = subprocess.run(["./test_008"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
        if run_res.returncode != 0:
            print("FAIL: Test execution failed")
            print(run_res.stdout)
            print(run_res.stderr)
            sys.exit(1)
        if "SUCCESS" not in run_res.stdout:
            print("FAIL: Execution output mismatch")
            sys.exit(1)
    finally:
        # cleanup
        for p in [Path("test_008"), Path("test_008.exe")]:
            if p.exists():
                try:
                    p.unlink()
                except:
                    pass

    # Ensure UserService::change_password was NOT modified to remove email (regression boundary)
    user_content = user_cpp.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if "send_email" not in user_content:
        print("FAIL: UserService::change_password should still send email notification directly")
        sys.exit(1)

    print("OK")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
